prompts.title: Form rhythm: victorias, empates y derrotas
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical frame on GoatLab charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 accents, slate #8ca6bf secondary. Reserve the lower quarter, full width, for permanent yellow subtitles; every graphic element stays above that band. Editorial variant leads the first half: kinetic typography with rhythmic emphasis. On beat one the Spanish team name "CR Flamengo" snaps in from the left as heavy condensed capitals, one word per beat, warm white, while a lime bar whips beneath it like a metronome. Beats two and three drop the Spanish result words "VICTORIAS", "EMPATES", "DERROTAS" as stacked type blocks that punch larger on the kick and settle, with a small slate tag reading "sin derrotas" landing on the third block. On beat four "Estudiantes de La Plata" arrives from the right in the same rhythm but denser and shorter, its blocks staggering slightly later so the cadence reads as uneven energy. No axes, no counts, no invented match events. Emphasis: a single lime flash on the "sin derrotas" tag. Transition: whip-pan blur into the statistical frame. Exit: all type compresses into a small lime stamp in the upper third, then dissolves. Statistical variant occupies the second half: grouped count bars, three bars per team, victorias, empates and derrotas, sharing one zero baseline and one common vertical scale in partidos. Gridlines in slate at low opacity, tick labels warm white, Spanish axis label "partidos". CR Flamengo bars in lime, Estudiantes de La Plata bars in slate, values {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}} printed at each bar tip with the unit word once per group. Entry: bars grow from the baseline in a short stagger, home group first. Main comparison: the derrotas bar of CR Flamengo stays at the baseline and pulses once while the away derrotas bar holds solid, a single focal point. Sample annotation under the chart names the sample explicitly, "muestra: {{home.n}} partidos · CR Flamengo / {{away.n}} partidos · Estudiantes de La Plata", with a source line "Fuente: Bzzoiro" in small slate type. Camera: subtle push-in toward the home group, no rotation. Exit: bars retract into the baseline, sample and source hold two frames, then a lime wipe transition.

prompts.title: Goles a favor y recibidos: cancha ilustrada
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical canvas, charcoal #101412 ground, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf accents. The lower quarter is reserved full width for permanent yellow subtitles; no chart element enters that band. Editorial variant opens the scene with an illustrative football pitch drawn in thin slate lines, top-down and slightly foreshortened to fill the upper two thirds of the frame. Spanish team names "CR Flamengo" and "Estudiantes de La Plata" sit at opposite ends in warm white capitals. Two lime ball trails arc across the pitch, abstract and deliberately non-literal, implying no scoreline and no specific move; each trail ends in a soft lime dot that pulses on the beat. On the second beat the trails cross, the pitch lines brighten, and a Spanish headline "GOLES A FAVOR Y EN CONTRA" rises with a slate underline. Emphasis: one focal pulse at the intersection. Transition: the two ball dots stretch into horizontal bars and fly downward, seeding the statistical chart. Exit: pitch lines fade while the headline lifts out through the top edge. Statistical variant fills the second half: paired horizontal bars, two rows per team, "Goles a favor" in lime and "Goles recibidos" in slate, on a shared zero baseline with one common scale in goles so both teams read on identical geometry. CR Flamengo shows {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}}; Estudiantes de La Plata shows {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}}, each printed at the bar tip with the unit "goles" appearing once per pair. Spanish team blocks label each pair; tick labels and the Spanish axis word "goles" sit in warm white over low-opacity slate gridlines. Entry: bars grow from the left baseline in a quick stagger, team labels fading in above each pair. Main comparison: a single synchronized highlight sweeps both lime favor bars, keeping one focal point. Under the chart a sample annotation reads "muestra reciente por equipo" with a source line "Fuente: Bzzoiro" in small slate type, both legible. Camera: gentle downward drift between the two team blocks, no zoom beyond a soft push. Exit: bars retract to zero, sample and source hold briefly, then a lime wipe transition into the next scene.

prompts.title: Arcos en cero: escudo defensivo
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical composition, charcoal #101412 base, warm white #edf0e6 typography, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf accents. Keep the lower quarter clear, full width, for permanent yellow subtitles; all graphics sit above it. Editorial variant leads with defensive energy and a stylised shield built from interlocking slate plates that assembles itself from the centre of the upper two thirds. As the plates click together, a lime core glows inside and the Spanish headline "ARCOS EN CERO" expands outward in condensed capitals, with the Spanish team names "CR Flamengo" and "Estudiantes de La Plata" appearing on either side of the shield in warm white. Small lime sparks fly on each plate impact, synced to the spoken rhythm, and the shield gives one firm lateral shove on the final beat, implying resistance without depicting any real save or match event. Emphasis: the lime core as the single focal point. Transition: the shield splits along its vertical seam and each half slides off-frame, revealing the chart. Exit: sparks decay, headline lifts away. Statistical variant: two count bars only, "Arcos en cero · CR Flamengo" at {{home.clean}} and "Arcos en cero · Estudiantes de La Plata" at {{away.clean}}, drawn on a shared zero baseline with one common scale in partidos. Counts stay counts: no conversion into rates, no fractions, no averages are shown anywhere. Bars are lime for the home side and slate for the away side, values printed at the tips with the unit word once. Entry: bars rise from the baseline in a slow confident stagger. Main comparison: the taller bar takes a single lime outline pulse while the shorter holds steady, preserving one focal point. Sample annotation sits under the chart, "muestra: {{home.n}} partidos · CR Flamengo / {{away.n}} partidos · Estudiantes de La Plata", with a source line "Fuente: Bzzoiro" in small slate type. Camera: slight lateral push from the away bar toward the home bar. Exit: bars settle, sample and source hold two frames, then a slate-to-lime wipe transition.

prompts.title: Cruces previos: duelo visual
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical frame, charcoal #101412 field, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf. The lower quarter stays reserved, full width, for permanent yellow subtitles; graphics never enter it. Editorial variant stages a visual duel: two vertical plates face each other across the centre line, the left one lime and carrying the Spanish name "CR Flamengo", the right one slate and carrying "Estudiantes de La Plata", both in condensed capitals. The plates advance on the beat, meet, and throw a thin lime spark across the gap; a Spanish headline "HISTORIAL" snaps above them and a slate ribbon reads "no es un pronóstico". Motion is a taut push-pull, plates leaning in and settling back twice, with the spark as the single focal point. No invented match events, no scoreline, no forecast. Transition: plates rotate edge-on and slice downward into the chart frame. Exit: spark cools, names drift to the corners. Statistical variant: one stacked horizontal bar representing the full head-to-head sample, total {{h2h.total}}, split into three proportional segments — "Victorias CR Flamengo" {{h2h.homeWins}} in lime, "Empates" {{h2h.draws}} in warm white, "Victorias Estudiantes de La Plata" {{h2h.awayWins}} in slate — with the three counts repeated as a grouped readout beneath and the unit word "partidos" once per value. Shared scale is the total sample, so segments sum to the bar and stay comparable. Entry: the bar draws from left to right, segments filling in sequence with thin dividers clicking into place. Main comparison: the lime and slate end segments get a gentle synchronized outline pulse while the middle holds, one focal point. Spanish labels stay legible at small sizes. Sample annotation under the bar reads "muestra: {{h2h.total}} cruces previos" with a source line "Fuente: Bzzoiro"; history only, no prediction implied. Camera: soft push-in on the bar centre. Exit: segments collapse into the total marker, sample and source linger, then a hard cut transition.

prompts.title: Síntesis: ataque visitante ante defensa local
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical scene, charcoal #101412 ground, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 for CR Flamengo, slate #8ca6bf for Estudiantes de La Plata. Reserve the lower quarter, full width, for permanent yellow subtitles; nothing else occupies that band. Editorial variant uses team reveals and narrative emphasis: two tall panels slide in from opposite edges of the frame, the lime-edged panel bearing the Spanish name "CR Flamengo" and the slate-edged panel bearing "Estudiantes de La Plata", both in heavy condensed capitals. They stop short of touching, leaving a narrow charcoal channel of light between them that widens slightly on the beat, and a Spanish phrase from the narration settles across the channel as warm white text — no numbers, no axes, no invented events. Emphasis: the channel of light as the single focal point, brightening once. Transition: the panels rotate to horizontal and fold down into two bars. Exit: panels recede to the edges and dim. Statistical variant states one grounded tension with compatible units: two horizontal bars on a shared zero baseline and one common scale in goles. The slate bar, labelled in Spanish "Estudiantes de La Plata · goles a favor", reads {{away.gf}}; the lime bar, labelled "CR Flamengo · goles recibidos", reads {{home.ga}}, with the unit word "goles" printed once per bar. No rates, no conversion, no projection, and no forecast claim: the frame shows counts only, explicitly captioned in Spanish as recent history rather than expectation. Entry: bars extend from the baseline with a whisper of stagger, labels fading in behind them. Main comparison: a single lime edge-light travels along the longer bar and stops, holding one focal point. Sample annotation beneath the pair reads "muestra: {{home.n}} partidos · CR Flamengo / {{away.n}} partidos · Estudiantes de La Plata", with a source line "Fuente: Bzzoiro" in small slate type. Camera: slow drift across the gap between the bars, never losing the labels. Exit: bars contract toward the centre, sample and source hold, then a lime curtain transition closes the montage.
